SMTO-AUT-0018 — SMTO can't find the Google app setup it needs

GUID: 40f7a625-6f1c-5912-9aa7-7a17cec7f031
Slug: google-oauth-app-missing
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: google-workspace

What happened

  • To connect to Google, SMTO needs a saved Google app setup (a Google Workspace OAuth App entry in Parameter Store). It couldn't find the one this request named, so it didn't contact Google.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store from the More options (⋯) menu and search for “google” to find an entry made from the Google Workspace OAuth App template. SMTO looks up the Google app setup by its exact name, so you need to know what it is called.
  2. If there is no such entry, ask the person who manages SMTO to create one: pick Google Workspace OAuth App in the template list, select New, add the client ID, and Save. This entry holds the app details Google needs before it will show you a sign-in page.
  3. Ask SMTO to connect your Google account and point it to that entry, for example by typing @ in the message box and picking the entry. SMTO doesn't guess between similar names; it uses only the exact entry you point it to.

What success looks like

  • SMTO gives you a Google sign-in link, and after you finish, the page says your email is connected and you can close the window.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. If a Google account used to work, don't delete or rename its Google app entry; the account depends on that exact name.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google OAuth application lookup failed: no google_oauth_app record exists at the requested exact key (or at the account's oauth_app_ref), or no Parameter Store was available to the Google provider.

What this means

  • Parameter resolution cannot find the selected Google OAuth application, or no Parameter Store is available to resolve it. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • Parameter resolution cannot find the selected Google OAuth application, or no Parameter Store is available to resolve it.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the exact application reference and whether its Parameter Store is available.

How to fix it

  • Create a google_oauth_app profile in Parameter Store (template "Google Workspace OAuth App") and pass its canonical key as auth_app_ref to auth.google_connect; aliases are not resolved. If a saved google_account fails to refresh with this error, restore a google_oauth_app at the key named in that account's oauth_app_ref. Google Calendar and Drive tools also need a Parameter Store in the execution context.
  • Save a Google Workspace OAuth App in Parameter Store and select its exact key.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm account identity and required features before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected application key resolves a valid Google OAuth App profile.

What not to do

  • Do not expose client secrets, tokens, codes or PKCE verifiers.
  • Do not switch accounts or repeat uncertain mutations automatically.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
